record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Prove or disprove the following statements about analytic capacity γ. (a) If E ⊆ C is compact and φ is a C 1 -diffeomorphism of C onto C, then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0. The statement is false if φ is a homeomorphism or a quasi-conformal mapping. (b) If E ⊆ C is compact and φ ∈ GL(2, R), then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0. (c) If E, F are compact subsets of C, then there exists a constant K > 0 (independent of the choice of E and F ) such that γ(E ∪ F ) ≤ K(γ(E) + γ(F )). Perhaps one can take K = 1? See [183] for related results. (d) If K is a compact subset of C with γ(K) = 0, then γ(E \ K) = γ(E) for all compact subsets E of C. Here γ(E \ K) means the inner capacity sup{γ(L) : L ⊆ E \ K, L compact}. An interesting special case would be that when K is the ‘corner quarters square Cantor set’ (the so-called Garnett set). (A. G. O’Farrell)

evidence.quote: Prove or disprove the following statements about analytic capacity γ. (a) If E ⊆ C is compact and φ is a C 1 -diffeomorphism of C onto C, then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0.
Part (c) is the same as Problem 7.39, which has been proved by Tolsa [752]. If E ⊂ R then γ(E) = 14 length(E), see Pommerenke [643].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let γ denote the analytic capacity on the complex plane: for a compact set E ⊆ ℂ,
   γ(E) = sup{ |f'(∞)| : f : ℂ∖E → ℂ bounded analytic, ‖f‖_∞ ≤ 1 },
where f'(∞) = lim_{z→∞} z(f(z) − f(∞)). For a non-compact set A ⊆ ℂ, define the inner analytic capacity by γ(A) = sup{ γ(L) : L ⊆ A, L compact }.

Prove or disprove each of the following statements.

(a) If E ⊆ ℂ is compact and φ : ℂ → ℂ is a C¹-diffeomorphism, then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0. (It is known that the analogue fails when φ is merely a homeomorphism, or merely a quasiconformal mapping.)

(b) If E ⊆ ℂ is compact and φ ∈ GL(2, ℝ) acts as a real-linear automorphism of ℂ ≅ ℝ², then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0.

(c) There exists an absolute constant K > 0 such that for all compact E, F ⊆ ℂ,
   γ(E ∪ F) ≤ K(γ(E) + γ(F)).
In particular, can one take K = 1?

(d) If K ⊆ ℂ is compact with γ(K) = 0, then γ(E ∖ K) = γ(E) for every compact E ⊆ ℂ, where γ(E ∖ K) is interpreted as the inner capacity defined above. A particularly interesting special case is when K is the "corner quarters" planar Cantor set (the Garnett set).
artifact.status_search_result: Part (c), the semiadditivity of analytic capacity, was proved by X. Tolsa (Acta Math. 190 (2003), 105–149) with some absolute constant K, settling Vitushkin's semiadditivity question; whether K = 1 is admissible remains open. Tolsa also established bilipschitz invariance of analytic capacity, which yields part (b) (linear maps are bilipschitz). Part (a) for general C¹-diffeomorphisms appears still open in the literature, and part (d) (the "subtraction of null sets") remains an open problem in general, including the Garnett set special case.

status_evidence.title: Painlevé's problem and the semiadditivity of analytic capacity
status_evidence.snippet: Tolsa proved the semiadditivity of analytic capacity: γ(E∪F) ≤ C(γ(E)+γ(F)) for an absolute constant C.
status_evidence.claim: Part (c) was proved by Tolsa with some constant K; the optimal value (in particular K=1) is not established.

status_evidence.title: Painlevé's problem, analytic capacity and curvature of measures (Tolsa, ECM)
status_evidence.snippet: Bilipschitz invariance of analytic capacity, solving a question of Verdera; C¹/diffeomorphism invariance remains discussed as an open issue.
status_evidence.claim: Bilipschitz invariance is established, implying invariance under GL(2,ℝ); the C¹-diffeomorphism case (a) is not resolved.
